hero.headline: U.S. attorney's office launches probe into California elections
hero.body:
Federal prosecutors in Los Angeles have opened an investigation into election fraud allegations connected to California's elections, the office announced as voters cast ballots in primary races statewide.

The announcement came as Californians selected party nominees for multiple offices, including the high-profile governor's race to replace outgoing Governor Gavin Newsom. The timing drew attention given the competitive nature of several contests on the ballot.

Federal prosecutors have the authority to investigate election crimes involving federal candidates or violations of federal law, including voter intimidation, ballot tampering, and certain types of fraud. When pursuing such investigations, U.S. attorney's offices typically work with state and local election officials. California uses a top-two primary system where all candidates appear on a single ballot, and the two candidates with the most votes advance to the general election regardless of party affiliation.

The Los Angeles office, which covers a jurisdiction including millions of voters across Southern California counties, provided no details about which specific races are under scrutiny or the nature of the alleged fraud being investigated.

Early results showed Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra leading in the governor's primary contest. The investigation comes as the justice department sent a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles county. State officials have rejected baseless claims about election integrity, though the delay in results immediately prompted misinformation about California's elections.

Federal election fraud prosecutions remain relatively uncommon, though the Justice Department maintains specialized units focused on election crimes. The U.S. attorney's office said it would provide updates as the investigation progresses.

California Secretary of State officials have not publicly commented on the federal probe. The state has implemented multiple election security measures in recent years, including risk-limiting audits and voter-verified paper trails for all ballots cast.

Experts have warned that ballot counting could extend beyond election day for the primary races involving the governor, Los Angeles mayor, and congressional seats. California's larger population and voting procedures have contributed to slower result reporting in recent election cycles.

The investigation represents the latest development in ongoing scrutiny of California's election processes at the federal level. The state, the nation's largest by population and a Democratic stronghold, has faced repeated claims about election integrity despite officials consistently rejecting such allegations.

The U.S. attorney's office has indicated it will release additional information about the investigation as it continues. Californians can expect the final results from the primary races to be released over the coming days as election officials complete ballot processing and verification procedures.

cards.headline: US and Iran exchange strikes in Gulf as ceasefire shows signs of strain
cards.body:
The United States and Iran clashed in the most serious test yet of their month-long ceasefire, with both sides accusing each other of violations as military exchanges erupted over the Persian Gulf on Thursday.

The US military said it intercepted multiple Iranian missiles, drones, and small boats targeting three American destroyers, the USS Truxtun, USS Rafael Peralta, and USS Mason, as they transited the Strait of Hormuz. American forces responded by striking Iranian military facilities, including missile and drone launch sites, command and control locations, and surveillance nodes. The Pentagon stated that no US assets were damaged in the attacks.

Iran's military disputed the American account, claiming the US violated the ceasefire by targeting an Iranian oil tanker and another vessel in the strait. Iranian officials said American airstrikes hit civilian areas along the coasts of Bandar Khamir, Sirik, and the island of Qeshm, which is home to approximately 150,000 people and a water desalination plant. Iran's armed forces responded by attacking US military vessels, with military officials claiming they inflicted significant damage, though the US denied this.

The strikes marked a troubling escalation for a ceasefire that has held for roughly a month. President Donald Trump downplayed the significance of the exchanges, describing the strikes as a "love tap" during remarks to reporters. He insisted the ceasefire remained intact despite the military action, though he acknowledged that a negotiated settlement "might not happen, but it could happen any day." Trump stated he believed Iran wanted a deal more than he did.

The confrontation came amid reports that the US and Iran had been approaching a temporary agreement to halt hostilities, with a one-page memorandum being shared between the two nations through Pakistan. However, senior Iranian officials have rejected recent concessions, with some analysts suggesting Iran may prefer prolonged negotiations closer to the November US midterm elections, when the Trump administration could face greater pressure to reach a settlement.

The exchanges occurred as the US has been enforcing a naval blockade to pressure Iran to reopen the strait. Earlier in the week, Trump sent warships to escort stranded tankers through the waterway in what he called "Project Freedom," during which the US military said it destroyed six Iranian boats along with cruise missiles and drones.

The latest flare-up raised questions about whether the ceasefire can withstand continued military provocations. Regional diplomats believe Iran risks overplaying its hand, as the current moment could offer an opportunity to end the conflict and claim victory, whereas resuming full-scale fighting might prove more costly. Meanwhile, crude oil prices climbed to approximately $101 per barrel following news of the attacks.

cards.headline: US Crude Oil Stockpiles Fall to Lowest Level Since 2004
cards.body:
US crude oil inventories have dropped to their lowest level in over two decades as the conflict with Iran continues to drain strategic reserves. The stockpiles posted their sixth consecutive weekly decline, bringing total reserves to levels not seen since 2004. The draw on US oil supplies comes as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has disrupted global oil flows.

The sharp reduction in crude inventories reflects both increased domestic consumption and the strategic decision to tap reserves amid the ongoing Iran conflict. The Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping channel through which nearly one-fifth of global oil passes, remains closed to commercial traffic. This has forced the US and other consuming nations to rely more heavily on their own stockpiles to meet demand.

Despite the significant supply shock, oil prices have not reached the extreme levels some analysts predicted. Industry observers note that several factors have prevented oil from reaching $200 per barrel, including demand adjustments, increased production from other sources, and strategic reserve releases coordinated among consuming nations. The current price environment reflects a complex interplay between physical supply constraints and market expectations about the duration of the crisis.

The depletion of US crude reserves raises questions about long-term energy security if the conflict extends further. Strategic petroleum reserves are designed to provide a buffer during supply disruptions, but sustained draws reduce the cushion available for future emergencies. Energy analysts are monitoring inventory levels closely as the government balances immediate supply needs against maintaining adequate reserves for potential future shocks.

The oil market situation adds economic pressure alongside the geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. While prices have remained below worst-case scenarios, the combination of low inventories and ongoing supply disruptions creates uncertainty for businesses and consumers. How long the US can sustain current draw rates from its strategic reserves while maintaining adequate emergency capacity remains a central question for policymakers and energy markets.

cards.headline: Trump Administration in Talks About Government Stakes in AI Companies
cards.teaser: The White House is discussing potential government equity positions in major artificial intelligence firms including OpenAI.
cards.body:
President Trump said his administration is discussing potential equity stakes in major AI companies like OpenAI. Trump framed the idea as a way for Americans to benefit from AI's success, describing it as "a beautiful thing." Administration officials may meet with AI firms in the coming weeks to explore the proposal.

The plan would represent an unusual shift in how the U.S. government engages with the technology sector. Supporters across the political spectrum have positioned government equity stakes as a form of universal basic capital, allowing citizens to share in AI industry gains. No specific financial terms or structural details have been announced yet.

cards.headline: Chip Stocks Drop Over $1 Trillion in Single-Day Selloff
cards.teaser: Semiconductor shares suffered their worst day in six years as investors pulled back from the sector.
cards.body:
The semiconductor sector lost between $1 trillion and $1.3 trillion in market value in a single trading session on Friday. Micron Technology shares fell 13 percent, while Nvidia, Broadcom, and Marvell also posted significant declines. The selloff marked the chip industry's worst day in six years, with analysts describing it as a cracking of Wall Street's hottest trade.

The sharp downturn affected companies across the semiconductor industry, from memory chip makers to designers of AI processors. Micron's double-digit percentage drop led losses among major chipmakers. The selloff raises questions about whether the recent rally in chip stocks had pushed valuations beyond sustainable levels, though the underlying drivers of the decline remain tied to broader market dynamics rather than company-specific news.

cards.headline: Trump pardons former GOP congressman convicted of insider trading
cards.teaser: President Trump granted a full pardon to ex-Representative Stephen Buyer, who was convicted of using nonpublic information to trade stocks after leaving office.
cards.body:
President Trump issued a pardon to former Representative Stephen Buyer of Indiana, who was convicted of insider trading for using nonpublic information to purchase stocks after his congressional tenure ended. The White House released a proclamation dated June 4 announcing the full, complete, and unconditional pardon.

The proclamation offered no explanation for the clemency decision. Buyer, a Republican who served in the House, faced criminal charges related to stock transactions made using information not available to the general public. The pardon wipes away his conviction and associated penalties.

cards.headline: Top White House artificial intelligence adviser departing administration
cards.teaser: Sriram Krishnan, a central figure in the Trump administration's AI policy efforts, is leaving his White House position but may continue advising on technology matters.
cards.body:
Sriram Krishnan, who has played a key role in shaping the administration's approach to artificial intelligence, will depart his White House advisory position. Krishnan has been instrumental in developing AI policy during his tenure with the Trump administration.

Despite leaving his formal White House role, Krishnan is expected to remain involved in the administration's technology initiatives. The departure represents a shift in the administration's AI leadership structure as the government continues to grapple with rapid advances in artificial intelligence and related regulatory questions.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones attack St Petersburg in strike Russia calls unprecedented
cards.teaser: Russian authorities urged residents to stay indoors for the first time since the war began as Ukrainian drones targeted the city.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones launched an attack on St Petersburg that Russian officials described as unprecedented in scale. The city's governor issued an urgent appeal for residents to remain indoors—the first such warning since the war began. The strike targeted Russia's second-largest city during President Putin's economic forum in his hometown.

In response, Putin announced plans to strengthen Russia's air defenses against the Ukrainian drone attacks, which have penetrated deep into Russian territory. The strikes represent a significant escalation in Ukraine's drone operations, bringing the conflict directly to major Russian urban centers.

cards.headline: Israeli strike kills three Lebanese soldiers including general in south Lebanon
cards.teaser: The Israeli military is investigating an attack that killed a Lebanese general and two other soldiers as Israeli forces fight Hezbollah in the region.
cards.body:
An Israeli military strike killed three Lebanese soldiers, including a general, in south Lebanon. The Israeli military confirmed hitting a vehicle and said the incident is being reviewed. Lebanon's President Joseph Aoun called the strike "a flagrant violation to Lebanese sovereignty and international law."

The attack occurred days after a ceasefire deal was signed. Israeli forces are conducting operations in south Lebanon against Hezbollah, an Iran-backed armed group, but the military offensive has affected others beyond its stated targets.

cards.headline: Israeli soldier kills seven-month-old baby in West Bank shooting
cards.teaser: An Israeli soldier fired at a vehicle in Hebron, killing an infant and wounding his parents, according to Palestinian health officials.
cards.body:
An Israeli soldier opened fire on a car in Hebron in the occupied West Bank on Friday, killing a seven-month-old baby and injuring his parents, according to Palestinian health officials. The Israeli military said the vehicle was speeding toward soldiers when one of them fired. The baby's grandmother, a passenger in the car, disputed this account of events.

The shooting represents part of a broader escalation in the West Bank, where Israeli military operations have intensified amid rising tensions. The Israeli military said the incident is under review and expressed "deep sorrow for any harm caused."

cards.headline: Defense Department raises threat assessment over Israeli espionage concerns
cards.teaser: The Pentagon increased its counterintelligence threat level to the highest rating amid concerns Israel eavesdropped on US-Iran negotiations.
cards.body:
The Defense Department has elevated its counterintelligence threat assessment to the highest level due to concerns about Israeli espionage activities. According to reports, Israel eavesdropped on American negotiations with Iran, prompting the reassessment of security protocols.

The increased threat level reflects the Pentagon's concerns about the compromise of sensitive diplomatic communications and intelligence sharing arrangements with Israel, a key U.S. ally in the Middle East.

cards.headline: Pope Leo begins Spain visit with call to reject polarization
cards.teaser: The pontiff urged Spanish leaders to stop fanning flames of division on his first papal visit to the country in 15 years.
cards.body:
Pope Leo XIV arrived in Spain on Saturday for a weeklong visit, his first to an EU country outside Italy. In his opening speech, the pontiff urged political leaders to seek unity rather than exploit divisions for political gain, and called on them to fight for peace.

The pope has prioritized meeting with marginalized communities during the tour, including homeless people in Madrid and migrants in the Canary Islands. This focus reflects his stated commitment to respecting every human being. The visit comes as Leo continues to take public stances on contemporary issues, including previous criticism of US President Donald Trump's immigration policies.

cards.headline: Hegseth invokes immigration in D-Day anniversary speech in France
cards.teaser: The defense secretary warned that Europe faces an invasion of dangerous ideologies during remarks at a World War II commemoration.
cards.body:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth drew parallels between the D-Day invasion and contemporary immigration during a speech at the Normandy anniversary commemoration in France. He warned that Europe faces threats from dangerous ideologies, comparing the historical military assault to modern migration patterns.

Hegseth attended the solemn ceremony with six of his children. His remarks departed from typical D-Day commemorations, which traditionally emphasize honoring veterans and the Allied victory over Nazi Germany rather than making commentary on current political issues.

hero.headline: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton enters Senate race
hero.teaser: Ken Paxton announced a bid for the U.S. Senate as his legal actions against Latino voting groups draw attention.

cards.headline: Republicans increasingly willing to oppose Trump agenda
cards.teaser: More Republican lawmakers are breaking with the president as midterm elections approach.
cards.body:
As November's midterm elections approach, Republican lawmakers are breaking ranks with President Trump more frequently. In recent weeks, small groups of GOP members have joined Democrats to advance war powers resolutions requiring congressional approval before continued hostilities against Iran. Republican dissenters have also supported additional aid for Ukraine.

The shift reflects lawmakers' calculations about their political survival. Facing potential electoral consequences in competitive districts, some Republicans are weighing loyalty to the administration against public opposition to certain policies. Trump's influence over congressional Republicans, while still significant, appears to be weakening as members prioritize their reelection prospects.

cards.headline: Pope Leo XIV says Iran war does not meet just war criteria
cards.teaser: The pontiff said the conflict in Iran does not qualify as a just war under Catholic teaching.
cards.body:
Pope Leo XIV stated that the conflict in Iran does not meet the criteria of a "just war" according to Catholic teaching. The pope made these remarks while speaking with journalists aboard the papal plane during his travel to Spain for a six-day visit.

Catholic doctrine on just war requires that military action satisfy specific moral standards, including legitimate authority, just cause, and proportionality. The pope's assessment directly addresses whether the war meets these established theological principles.

cards.headline: Ukrainian drones strike St. Petersburg in major attack
cards.teaser: Russia called the assault on the city unprecedented as the governor urged residents to stay indoors.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones launched an attack on St. Petersburg that Russian officials called unprecedented. The city's governor issued an advisory urging residents to remain indoors—the first such warning since the war began.

The strikes represent a significant escalation in Ukrainian drone operations targeting deep inside Russian territory. President Putin responded by saying Russia would strengthen its air defenses in response to the attacks, which he noted had disrupted his economic forum in the city.

cards.headline: Teenager Mirra Andreeva wins French Open title
cards.teaser: The young Russian player captured her first Grand Slam championship with a victory over Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska.
cards.body:
Teenager Mirra Andreeva won her first Grand Slam title at the French Open, defeating Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska in the final. The victory fulfills expectations that Andreeva would become a major force in professional tennis.

Chwalinska's remarkable run to the final as a qualifier came to an end with the loss, denying her a fairytale French Open triumph. Andreeva's breakthrough win marks a significant moment in her young career.

cards.headline: West Ham chairman David Sullivan steps down over historic allegations
cards.teaser: Sullivan resigned immediately as joint chairman after being informed of impending publication of serious allegations.
cards.body:
West Ham United joint chairman David Sullivan has stepped down from his position with immediate effect. The move came after he was informed that serious historic allegations about his behaviour were about to be published.

Sullivan had served as joint chairman alongside David Gold until Gold's death in 2023. The allegations were uncovered in a joint investigation by BBC Panorama and the Times newspaper.

cards.headline: England advances toward Test victory over New Zealand at Lord's
cards.teaser: Rain limited play on the third day, but England made progress toward a much-needed win in the first Test.
cards.body:
England moved closer to victory over New Zealand on day three of the first Test at Lord's, despite heavy rain severely limiting play. Just 58 legal deliveries were possible as wet conditions repeatedly interrupted proceedings and pushed England's path to victory into the fourth day.

The rain-affected day allowed England to make use of the brief windows of available playing time to strengthen their position in the match. The weather continued to disrupt the schedule, with players taking an early lunch as conditions remained uncertain throughout the day.

cards.headline: SpaceX IPO Subscription Doubles Initial Offering Size
cards.teaser: Demand for shares in Elon Musk's space company has exceeded the initial public offering by a factor of two.
cards.body:
The SpaceX initial public offering is set for June 12 with a valuation of $135 per share. The company plans to sell 555.6 million shares, raising $75 billion in what would be the largest stock market launch in history. Up to a quarter of the shares will be reserved for individual investors, a larger retail allocation than typical for major IPOs.

The offering has attracted substantial interest from both institutional and retail investors. However, market experts have raised concerns about potential risks for individual buyers entering at the IPO price.

cards.headline: Paramount Offers to Sell Children's Channels to Win EU Approval for Warner Deal
cards.teaser: The media company is proposing asset sales to address European competition concerns over the $110 billion merger.
cards.body:
Paramount has offered to divest certain children's television channels as a concession to European regulators examining its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. The European Union has expressed concerns about market concentration in specific programming segments resulting from the merger.

The deal faces scrutiny from competition authorities on both sides of the Atlantic. In the United States, multiple states are preparing lawsuits to block the combination. Paramount has separately asked a judge to dismiss a consumer antitrust lawsuit challenging the Warner Bros. Discovery merger.

cards.headline: Cattle Ranchers Face Screwworm Threat and Drought Conditions
cards.teaser: Texas livestock producers are dealing with the possibility of a screwworm outbreak while other regions lack sufficient grazing grass.
cards.body:
Screwworm Flies Add to Cattle Ranchers' Woes

Texas cattle ranchers face mounting concerns as screwworm outbreaks threaten livestock operations. A second infected calf was identified in the state, prompting Texas to declare a disaster. The severity of the threat prompted Canada to ban imports of Texas cattle.

Ranchers contend with multiple pressures beyond disease. Drought has reduced available forage in cattle-raising regions, forcing producers to send animals to market sooner than planned. Early sales limit the weights ranchers can achieve before marketing, reducing potential revenues and compounding financial strain on livestock operations.

cards.headline: Elon Musk Leads Executive Compensation Rankings
cards.teaser: The Tesla and SpaceX CEO appears at the top of a list of highest-paid chief executives at major companies.
cards.body:
Elon Musk dominates the latest rankings of CEO compensation at the largest US companies by revenue. His pay packages at both Tesla and SpaceX have reshaped discussions about executive compensation structures. After facing legal challenges to his Tesla compensation plan, Musk designed his SpaceX pay agreement with different provisions aimed at withstanding judicial scrutiny.

The structure of Musk's compensation has influenced broader trends in how companies design executive pay packages. His performance-based awards, which can reach into the hundreds of billions or trillions of dollars if certain milestones are met, represent a departure from traditional salary and bonus arrangements. Corporate governance experts continue to debate whether such arrangements align executive and shareholder interests or represent excessive payouts.

hero.headline: AI scans 35 years of Hubble images, discovers over 800 undocumented objects
hero.body:
An artificial intelligence system has identified more than 800 previously unknown objects by analyzing 35 years of images from the Hubble Space Telescope, revealing that one of astronomy's most extensively studied archives still contains hidden discoveries.

The AI analyzed the complete collection of images captured by Hubble since its launch in 1990, systematically searching through data that would be too vast for human researchers to review manually. The telescope has collected millions of images over its operational lifetime, creating an archive of such scale that traditional review methods cannot examine every frame comprehensively.

The newly discovered objects represent various astronomical phenomena that were present in archived images but had not been previously cataloged or documented in scientific literature. While specific details about the types of objects remain unclear, the sheer number of finds indicates that numerous categories of celestial bodies and events went unnoticed during initial image reviews.

Hubble operates from an orbit approximately 340 miles above Earth's surface and captures images across visible, ultraviolet, and near-infrared wavelengths. Since its deployment, the telescope has become one of the most productive scientific instruments ever created, with its images supporting thousands of published research papers. Astronomers worldwide rely on the Hubble archive for studies ranging from nearby planets to the most distant galaxies.

The application of artificial intelligence to examine existing astronomical data represents a growing trend as the field confronts increasingly large datasets. Modern telescopes generate vast collections of information that exceed the capacity of traditional analysis methods. Automated systems can process these enormous archives systematically, identifying phenomena and patterns that might otherwise remain concealed for years or decades.

This discovery at Hubble suggests that similar long-running observational programs may also contain substantial amounts of unexplored information within their existing archives. As technology advances and new analytical approaches emerge, previously overlooked discoveries may surface from datasets collected years or even decades ago.

The findings underscore a significant limitation in conventional astronomical research: even the most thoroughly studied collections of observations can contain undiscovered content. While human researchers carefully examine images when they are first collected, the scale of modern astronomical data means some discoveries inevitably escape initial attention.

The success of AI analysis in uncovering these objects suggests that future approaches to astronomical data will increasingly rely on automated systems working alongside human expertise. As telescopes continue generating larger volumes of information, combining human knowledge with machine learning capabilities offers a powerful method for extracting maximum scientific value from observational programs. The Hubble discovery demonstrates that the universe still holds secrets even in data that scientists have examined countless times.

cards.headline: Apple prepares iOS 27 with new Siri features for developer conference
cards.teaser: Apple plans to unveil iOS 27 at its annual developer conference, with updates focused on artificial intelligence and Siri improvements.
cards.body:
Apple is set to announce iOS 27 at its Worldwide Developers Conference, with the event showcasing updates centered on Siri and AI integration. The presentation will highlight how Apple incorporates artificial intelligence technology into its operating systems, including both iOS 27 and macOS 27.

The conference marks a significant milestone for CEO Tim Cook, who is holding his final developer event in his role. The new Siri represents Apple's effort to strengthen its AI capabilities after falling behind competitors in recent years.

cards.headline: Researchers find ancient microbes frozen with Ötzi the Iceman can still grow
cards.teaser: Microorganisms preserved alongside the 5,300-year-old mummy have demonstrated the ability to continue growing after millennia in ice.
cards.body:
Scientists studying the Iceman mummy discovered that some ancient microbes frozen with the remains retain the capacity for growth. The finding raises questions about the preservation of biological material in ice and the boundary between artifacts and living ecosystems.

Ötzi, a naturally mummified human who died approximately 5,300 years ago, was found in the Alps in 1991. The body's preservation in ice maintained not only human tissue but also microorganisms present at the time of death. Researchers have now confirmed that some of these microbial samples can still reproduce under laboratory conditions.

cards.headline: Air filters capture floating DNA that identifies nearby wildlife and viruses
cards.teaser: Scientists have found that standard air filtration systems collect environmental DNA that can reveal the presence of animals, plants, and pathogens in surrounding areas.
cards.body:
Scientists have discovered that air filters can capture DNA fragments floating in the atmosphere. This genetic material, shed by living organisms, becomes airborne and gets trapped in ventilation systems, allowing researchers to analyze it.

The captured DNA can identify wildlife, viruses, and vegetation in the area surrounding the air intake. The technique can even detect plants associated with drug production nearby, opening new possibilities for environmental monitoring and surveillance.

cards.headline: Sea star populations show baby boom after massive die-off
cards.teaser: A biologist observing sea star populations has documented a surge in juvenile specimens following a widespread mortality event.
cards.body:
Sea star populations are experiencing a significant increase in young specimens after suffering through a massive die-off. A biologist monitoring the recovery has observed reproduction rates that exceed expectations for the species.

The die-off reduced sea star numbers across affected coastal areas, raising concerns about the species' ability to recover. The subsequent baby boom suggests the populations are rebounding, though the long-term trajectory of the recovery remains under observation.

cards.headline: Spain prepares for first of three eclipses arriving this summer
cards.teaser: Spain will experience three eclipses in the coming period, with the first visible this summer and offering viewing opportunities across the country.
cards.body:
Spain is preparing for the first of three upcoming eclipses, scheduled for this summer. The August event will provide viewing opportunities in several locations, including vineyard regions popular with tourists.

The 2026 total solar eclipse serves as a preview for a longer eclipse in 2027, which will produce six minutes and 23 seconds of darkness. Multiple locations near major Spanish vacation destinations offer accessible viewing points for the summer eclipse. The 2027 event is projected to be the longest total solar eclipse of the century.

cards.headline: Sriram Krishnan steps down as White House AI advisor
cards.teaser: Krishnan is leaving his position advising the administration on artificial intelligence policy and plans to establish a new organization.
cards.body:
Sriram Krishnan is departing his role as AI advisor to the White House. He reportedly plans to launch a new institution focused on continuing to influence the Trump administration's approach to artificial intelligence policy.

Krishnan's tenure involved shaping federal policy on AI development and regulation. His new organization will allow him to maintain involvement in policy discussions from outside the government structure.

hero.headline: Russian teenager Andreeva wins French Open for first Grand Slam title
hero.body:
Mirra Andreeva claimed her first Grand Slam title at the French Open, defeating Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska in the women's final. The Russian teenager fulfilled her potential on the clay courts of Roland Garros, ending Chwalinska's remarkable run through the tournament.

Chwalinska had surprised the tennis world by reaching the final as a qualifier, making her own fairytale journey through the draw. The Polish player had overcome multiple higher-ranked opponents to reach her first Grand Slam final, but fell short against Andreeva in the championship match.

The victory marks a breakthrough moment for Andreeva, who had shown promise in previous major tournaments but had not yet secured a Grand Slam title. The teenager displayed composure beyond her years to claim the trophy at one of tennis's most prestigious events. Her win on the red clay in Paris establishes her as a rising force in women's tennis.

Andreeva's triumph continues a strong tradition of young players making their mark at the French Open. The tournament has historically provided a platform for emerging talents to announce themselves on the global stage, and Andreeva joins that list with her championship victory. Her aggressive style of play and mental toughness proved decisive in the final.

The championship concludes a memorable tournament that saw Chwalinska's unexpected path to the final capture attention across the sport. While the qualifier's run ended without the title, her performance throughout the two weeks in Paris marked a significant achievement. For Andreeva, the Grand Slam trophy represents the realization of years of development and establishes her as one of the sport's brightest young stars.

cards.headline: Antonelli takes pole position at Monaco Grand Prix ahead of Verstappen
cards.teaser: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli secured pole position for the Monaco Grand Prix, beating Red Bull's Max Verstappen in qualifying.
cards.body:
Kimi Antonelli claimed pole position at the Monaco Grand Prix, edging out Max Verstappen by 0.043 seconds in a tightly contested qualifying session. The 19-year-old Mercedes driver delivered a flawless lap to secure the top spot on the challenging street circuit, fending off efforts from Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, whose combined titles span 11 championships.

Hamilton qualified third in his Ferrari, with George Russell sixth for the team. The narrow margins and intensity of the session underscored Antonelli's performance on one of Formula One's most demanding single-lap challenges. Qualifying proved decisive at Monaco, where overtaking remains nearly impossible on race day.

cards.headline: England close in on Test victory over New Zealand at Lord's
cards.teaser: England moved closer to a first Test win over New Zealand despite rain limiting play on day three at Lord's.
cards.body:
England moved closer to victory over New Zealand on a rain-affected third day of the first Test at Lord's. Ollie Robinson was instrumental with the ball, taking two wickets to strengthen the hosts' position in the match.

Persistent wet weather interrupted play throughout the day, limiting the time available for either side to build momentum. Despite the weather challenges, England made progress toward what would be a much-needed Test victory as the match headed toward its final days.

cards.headline: Wembanyama acknowledges mistakes in Spurs' Game 2 NBA Finals loss
cards.teaser: Victor Wembanyama took responsibility for late-game errors that contributed to the San Antonio Spurs' loss in Game 2 of the NBA Finals.
cards.body:
Victor Wembanyama took responsibility for costly late-game errors after the San Antonio Spurs fell to the New York Knicks 105-104 in Game 2 of the NBA Finals. The young star's mistakes down the stretch proved decisive in the one-point defeat.

The loss leaves the Spurs in a dire position, trailing 2-0 as the series shifts to New York. The Knicks are now two wins away from capturing their first championship in generations. San Antonio must regroup quickly to avoid falling further behind against the hot Knicks team.

cards.headline: Exeter reach Premiership playoffs with win over Saracens
cards.teaser: Exeter defeated Saracens 32-12 to secure a Premiership playoff semi-final spot and end Mark McCall's tenure as Saracens head coach.
cards.body:
Exeter beat Saracens 32-12 to secure a Premiership playoff semi-final spot, marking their return to the top four for the first time since 2021. The victory over their bitter rivals was celebrated with particular intensity by the home crowd at Sandy Park.

The result also marks the end of Mark McCall's 15-year tenure as Saracens director of rugby. Exeter will now face Bath in the semi-final at the Rec, where Bath secured a home tie with their own win over Leicester.

cards.headline: Bath secure home Premiership semi-final with victory over Leicester
cards.teaser: Bath held on to beat Leicester Tigers, securing second place and a home semi-final against Exeter Chiefs in the Premiership playoffs.
cards.body:
Bath defeated Leicester Tigers 24-22 to secure second place in the Premiership and earn a home semi-final. The defending champions will face Exeter Chiefs next week, while Leicester travels to Northampton.

The victory was built on Du Toit's hat-trick as Bath held on in a bruising encounter with their fierce rivals. The win sets up two semi-final derbies, with Bath hosting Exeter and Northampton taking on Leicester.

cards.headline: Bulls rally from 18 points down to beat Glasgow in URC semi-final
cards.teaser: The Bulls recovered from an 18-point deficit to defeat Glasgow Warriors in the United Rugby Championship playoff semi-final.
cards.body:
Glasgow Warriors suffered playoff heartbreak as the Bulls mounted a stunning comeback from 18 points down to win the URC semi-final. The South African side's dramatic fightback secured their place in the final.

Glasgow had built a commanding lead but could not hold on as the Bulls battled back. The loss extends Glasgow's playoff struggles and ends their season.

hero.headline: Backrooms Set to Become A24's Highest-Grossing Film Worldwide
hero.teaser: The A24 horror film Backrooms is on track to surpass Marty Supreme as the studio's highest-grossing movie ever at the global box office.
hero.body:
The horror film Backrooms is on track to surpass Marty Supreme's $191 million worldwide total, marking a significant achievement for the independent studio A24. The movie's strong performance at the box office demonstrates the studio's ability to produce both critically respected and commercially viable films.

Director Kane Parsons, who is 20 years old, created the film by adapting a horror concept that originated in internet culture. His work on Backrooms represents a notable example of how online creative communities are now influencing major film productions.

The success of Backrooms, combined with another recent A24 release called Obsession, has drawn attention to a broader trend in the entertainment industry. Multiple sources have highlighted how YouTube creators and internet personalities are gaining increased influence in Hollywood. This shift reflects changing patterns in where filmmakers and talent are emerging from, as traditional industry pathways compete with digital platforms for recognition and opportunity.

Industry observers have also noted that Backrooms and similar recent releases signal what some are calling a horror renaissance aimed at younger audiences. This generation of viewers appears to have distinct preferences that differ from previous demographics, and studios are responding by developing content that appeals to their sensibilities and interests.

The film's production itself became part of its public narrative. According to reports, the filming process was so immersive and complex that even crew members found themselves disoriented on set, adding to the behind-the-scenes mystique surrounding the project.

Parsons' achievement at such a young age has generated considerable media interest. Profile pieces and retrospectives about the director have appeared across major entertainment publications, reflecting the novelty and appeal of his rapid rise in the industry.

A24's track record with Backrooms and Obsession suggests that the studio has successfully identified and capitalized on emerging audience tastes. Rather than relying solely on established franchises or star power, the studio backed projects rooted in contemporary internet culture and directed by young, digitally native creators.

This combination of factors—a young director adapting internet phenomena, content aimed at Gen Z audiences, and the involvement of YouTube creators—appears to represent a shift in how major studios are developing and greenighting films. The commercial success of Backrooms validates this approach and may influence how other studios approach their development strategies going forward.

The film's performance suggests that audiences are receptive to horror content that speaks directly to their cultural references and online experiences. As Backrooms moves closer to becoming A24's highest-grossing release, it serves as a marker of this changing landscape in filmmaking and entertainment production.

cards.headline: Patrick Godfrey, Actor Who Played Leonardo da Vinci in Ever After, Dies at 93
cards.teaser: Patrick Godfrey, the English actor known for portraying Leonardo da Vinci in the 1998 film Ever After: A Cinderella Story, died Thursday.
cards.body:
Patrick Godfrey, an English actor best known for portraying Leonardo da Vinci in the 1998 fantasy film "Ever After: A Cinderella Story," has died at 93. His death was announced on June 5 by his talent agency, Markham Froggatt Irwin.

In "Ever After," a reimagined take on the Cinderella fairy tale starring Drew Barrymore, Godfrey's performance as the Renaissance polymath helped ground the classic story in a historical setting. The veteran actor had a long career spanning both film and theater.

cards.headline: Scary Movie 6 Opens to $24.7 Million on Friday, Sets Franchise Record
cards.teaser: Scary Movie 6 earned $24.7 million at the domestic box office on Friday, positioning the film for what is expected to be the biggest opening weekend in the fran.
cards.body:
Scary Movie 6 earned $24.7 million at the domestic box office on Friday, positioning the film for what is expected to be the biggest opening weekend in the franchise's history. The Paramount and Miramax release played in 3,490 theaters and is projected to finish the weekend with over $50 million in ticket sales.

The film marks the first entry in the parody series directed by the Wayans brothers since Scary Movie 2 in 2001. The horror-comedy franchise, which began in 2000, has produced five previous installments that collectively grossed hundreds of millions of dollars worldwide. The return of the Wayans brothers appears to have revitalized interest in the series after a 25-year gap in their involvement.

Masters of the Universe claimed the second position at the box office with $11.7 million on Friday. The film is expected to finish the weekend with approximately $31 million. The competition between the two releases illustrates the continued strength of both comedy and action-adventure genres at theaters.

Backrooms, an A24 release, continues to perform beyond expectations and is on track to become the studio's highest-grossing film ever worldwide. The movie is set to surpass the $191 million global total of Marty Supreme, which previously held the record for A24. The success of Backrooms demonstrates the expanding appeal of horror content adapted from internet culture.

The strong opening for Scary Movie 6 reflects broader trends in theatrical releases, where established franchises with returning creative talent can still draw substantial audiences. The film's performance suggests that audiences remain interested in theatrical comedy experiences despite the proliferation of streaming options. Industry observers will watch closely to see whether the opening weekend momentum carries through the following weeks.

cards.headline: Bruce Springsteen Performs With Jon Bon Jovi and Public Enemy at Music America Concert
cards.teaser: Bruce Springsteen appeared with Jon Bon Jovi and Public Enemy at the second night of the Songs that Shaped Us concert series.
cards.body:
The performance took place at the final Music America concert, where Springsteen covered songs by Elvis Presley, Bob Dylan, Eddie Floyd, and Southside Johnny. The show featured collaborations between multiple artists as part of the multi-night event.

Springsteen closed his set with one of his own songs after performing the series of covers. The Songs that Shaped Us concert series brought together musicians to celebrate influential tracks from American music history.

cards.headline: AMC Relaunches Interview With the Vampire as The Vampire Lestat
cards.teaser: AMC is transforming its Interview With the Vampire series into The Vampire Lestat, featuring a rock concert format and 20 original songs.
cards.body:
The network held a premiere party for The Vampire Lestat at New York's Beacon Theatre on June 2, where actor Sam Reid performed six original songs in character as the vampire-turned-rocker Lestat de Lioncourt. Reid, who does not perform professionally as a musician, took on the role of the rock star vampire for the series relaunch.

The show's transformation includes major marketing tie-ins and a concert-centered narrative. The rebranding represents a shift in the series' format and storytelling approach, moving the focus to the character of Lestat and incorporating musical performance as a central element.

cards.headline: House of the Dragon Season 3 to Open With Battle of the Gullet
cards.teaser: The third season of House of the Dragon will begin with the Battle of the Gullet, described by showrunner Ryan Condal as a television first.
cards.body:
Condal, who serves as showrunner and co-creator of the Game of Thrones prequel series, told an audience at Shoreditch Town Hall in East London that the battle sequence represents something unprecedented in television production. He stated that Season 3 would deliver on promises made in the preceding season.

The Battle of the Gullet is a major naval conflict from the source material that kicks off the new season. Condal characterized the sequence as unlike anything previously attempted on television, suggesting a significant investment in the production's scale and visual effects.

cards.headline: Masters of the Universe Composer Uses Brian May's Guitar for Film Score
cards.teaser: Daniel Pemberton created the Masters of the Universe theme using Brian May's Red Special guitar, drawing inspiration from Queen and ABBA.
cards.body:
Pemberton, who typically avoids franchise films and sequels, agreed to score the new Masters of the Universe film after director Travis Knight confirmed he wanted Queen and ABBA-inspired music. The approach aligned with Pemberton's vision for creating what he described as unashamedly fun music.

The composer recorded parts of the score using May's signature Red Special guitar, the instrument the Queen guitarist built with his father and has used throughout his career. The musical direction represents a deliberate choice to evoke the sound of 1970s and 1980s rock and pop.

hero.headline: U.S. attorney's office launches probe into California elections
hero.body:
Federal prosecutors in Los Angeles have opened an investigation into election fraud allegations connected to California's elections, the office announced as voters cast ballots in primary races statewide.

The announcement came as Californians selected party nominees for multiple offices, including the high-profile governor's race to replace outgoing Governor Gavin Newsom. The timing drew attention given the competitive nature of several contests on the ballot.

Federal prosecutors have the authority to investigate election crimes involving federal candidates or violations of federal law, including voter intimidation, ballot tampering, and certain types of fraud. When pursuing such investigations, U.S. attorney's offices typically work with state and local election officials. California uses a top-two primary system where all candidates appear on a single ballot, and the two candidates with the most votes advance to the general election regardless of party affiliation.

The Los Angeles office, which covers a jurisdiction including millions of voters across Southern California counties, provided no details about which specific races are under scrutiny or the nature of the alleged fraud being investigated.

Early results showed Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra leading in the governor's primary contest. The investigation comes as the justice department sent a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles county. State officials have rejected baseless claims about election integrity, though the delay in results immediately prompted misinformation about California's elections.

Federal election fraud prosecutions remain relatively uncommon, though the Justice Department maintains specialized units focused on election crimes. The U.S. attorney's office said it would provide updates as the investigation progresses.

California Secretary of State officials have not publicly commented on the federal probe. The state has implemented multiple election security measures in recent years, including risk-limiting audits and voter-verified paper trails for all ballots cast.

Experts have warned that ballot counting could extend beyond election day for the primary races involving the governor, Los Angeles mayor, and congressional seats. California's larger population and voting procedures have contributed to slower result reporting in recent election cycles.

The investigation represents the latest development in ongoing scrutiny of California's election processes at the federal level. The state, the nation's largest by population and a Democratic stronghold, has faced repeated claims about election integrity despite officials consistently rejecting such allegations.

The U.S. attorney's office has indicated it will release additional information about the investigation as it continues. Californians can expect the final results from the primary races to be released over the coming days as election officials complete ballot processing and verification procedures.

cards.headline: Trump pardons former GOP congressman convicted of insider trading
cards.teaser: President Trump granted a full pardon to ex-Representative Stephen Buyer, who was convicted of using nonpublic information to trade stocks after leaving office.
cards.body:
President Trump issued a pardon to former Representative Stephen Buyer of Indiana, who was convicted of insider trading for using nonpublic information to purchase stocks after his congressional tenure ended. The White House released a proclamation dated June 4 announcing the full, complete, and unconditional pardon.

The proclamation offered no explanation for the clemency decision. Buyer, a Republican who served in the House, faced criminal charges related to stock transactions made using information not available to the general public. The pardon wipes away his conviction and associated penalties.

cards.headline: Top White House artificial intelligence adviser departing administration
cards.teaser: Sriram Krishnan, a central figure in the Trump administration's AI policy efforts, is leaving his White House position but may continue advising on technology matters.
cards.body:
Sriram Krishnan, who has played a key role in shaping the administration's approach to artificial intelligence, will depart his White House advisory position. Krishnan has been instrumental in developing AI policy during his tenure with the Trump administration.

Despite leaving his formal White House role, Krishnan is expected to remain involved in the administration's technology initiatives. The departure represents a shift in the administration's AI leadership structure as the government continues to grapple with rapid advances in artificial intelligence and related regulatory questions.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland secured the Democratic nomination for New Mexico governor and could become the first female Native American governor if elected.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for New Mexico governor. The former Interior Secretary in the Biden administration previously represented New Mexico in Congress before joining the cabinet.

If elected in the general election, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor of a state.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead in early California governor primary results
cards.teaser: Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are ahead in preliminary returns from California's gubernatorial primary to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Early results from California's governor primary show Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra leading their respective fields. The race includes Democrats Katie Porter and Tom Steyer, while Republican Chad Bianco also competes for his party's nomination to replace outgoing Governor Gavin Newsom.

California's top-two primary system allows the two highest vote-getters to advance to the general election regardless of party. Vote counting continues across the state, with the US Justice Department sending a federal prosecutor to observe ballot processing in Los Angeles as results are tallied.

cards.headline: Susan Collins calls allegations against Democratic rival troubling
cards.teaser: Senator Susan Collins of Maine described new allegations against Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner as troubling ahead of upcoming primaries.
cards.body:
Senator Susan Collins commented on mounting allegations surrounding Graham Platner, the progressive oyster farmer expected to be her Democratic opponent in Maine's Senate race. Collins characterized the latest claims against Platner as troubling as voters prepare for the state's Senate primaries.

Platner returned to campaigning Friday following a day away from the trail amid increased scrutiny of his background. He expressed defiance in response to the allegations, saying Maine has his back. The primaries will determine which candidates advance to face Collins in the general election.

cards.headline: Bill Maher jokes about tracking Trump's mood through social media attacks
cards.teaser: Comedian Bill Maher said he gauges President Trump's temperament by whether the president is criticizing him on social media platforms.
cards.body:
Bill Maher joked on his HBO show Friday that he can gauge President Trump's temperament by monitoring his social media attacks. The comedian said he knows when Trump is in a bad mood because the president starts tweeting about him, referencing a pattern of presidential attacks directed at him personally.

Maher suggested Trump's approval ratings have affected the president's mood and tweeting behavior. The comedian's show has regularly featured political commentary on the Trump administration.
